content_voiceover: This slide covers the Evans staging system for liver tumors, which is based on clinical evaluation by the surgeon and pathological findings at resection, in contrast to the imaging-based PRETEXT system you'll see next. Stage one is complete surgical resection with a margin free from tumor. Stage two is gross resection but with microscopic residual disease left behind. Stage three is gross resection with macroscopic residual disease, meaning visible tumor remains. And stage four is distant metastases. The diagrams below illustrate the Couinaud segmental anatomy of the liver, which underlies both the Evans system and the PRETEXT system, dividing the liver into the right posterior section, segments six and seven, the right anterior section, segments five and eight, the left medial section, segment four, and the left lateral section, segments two and three. Understanding these four sections is essential because PRETEXT staging, which we'll cover next, counts how many of these four contiguous sections are tumor-free rather than relying on surgical outcome, and that distinction, surgical staging versus radiographic staging, is a common board discrimination point.
keypoints: Evans staging is based on surgical and pathological findings, not imaging
Stage I: complete resection, margins tumor-free
Stage II: gross resection, microscopic residual disease
Stage III: gross resection, macroscopic residual disease
Stage IV: distant metastases; liver divided into 4 sections for staging
keypoint_voiceover: Evans staging is a post-surgical system, Stage one is complete resection with clear margins, Stage two has microscopic residual disease, Stage three has macroscopic residual disease, and Stage four is distant metastasis. The liver's four sections, right posterior, right anterior, left medial, and left lateral, form the anatomic basis for both Evans and PRETEXT staging.
